text:
Priya: Quick sync — proposing a 'watchtower' service that sits between telemetry and the routing layer to own automatic fallback decisions for canaries. thinking probe+decide+act separation. thoughts?
Sam: +1 to separation. we need clear boundaries: who writes the decision rules vs who executes rollbacks. also how do we test the actuator safely? :eyes:
Ethan: Suggestion: decision logic = control-plane stateless component (can be tested with recorded metrics), actuator = single RPC surface that only routing team owns. watchtower emits a signed 'fallback intent' that actuator must validate. keeps blast radius small.
Kari: Important: auto-fallback for perf regressions is ok; for correctness/regression in outputs we should require manual approval or stronger signals. we should define signal types: perf vs correctness vs infra.
oncall-bot: [alert] Canary v3 at 5% -> p99 latency bumped to 1.8s over 3m (threshold 1.4s)
deploy-bot: Canary start: v3 -> 5% traffic. canary_id=canary-32100055
Priya: good point on signal types. proposal: watchtower evaluates named signals and maps to policies. sample policy language:```yaml
- name: perf-fallback
  signals:
    - metric: p99_latency
      aggregator: rolling_5m
      op: '>'
      value: 1.5
  action: fallback_to: stable-v2
  auto: true
- name: correctness-block
  signals:
    - metric: human-eval-fail_rate
      aggregator: rolling_30m
      op: '>'
      value: 0.01
  action: pause-and-alert
  auto: false
window: 5m
```
Sam: That format is good. A few tradeoffs: 1) auto:true reduces MTTR but increases risk of false positives. need cooldowns and hysteresis. 2) actor needs idempotent rollback APIs. 3) we must record decisions in audit log.
Ethan: Add policy fields: min_lookback, cooldown_secs, required_signals (e.g., both error_rate AND p99). watchtower should support composite predicates.
Kari: Also require a human override TTL so oncall can block automatic fallback for a given canary if investigating. CLI: `watchtower block --canary canary-32100055 --reason "investigating" --ttl 30m`
Priya: For verification: we can run decision engine in dry-run against historical traces to compute expected false positive rate. include that in rollout checklist.
oncall-bot: [note] dry-run result: simulated policy perf-fallback would have triggered 2 rollbacks in last 14 days (both correlated with infra blips)
Sam: Ops/ownership: control-plane team owns watchtower code, routing/gateway team owns actuator APIs, oncall owns runbook content and thresholds for auto:true. add product/ML for correctness signals.
Ethan: Implementation detail: watchtower should write decisions to durable queue (audit + replay). actuator reads decisions and performs CAS on route config, exposing `rollback_id` and `reason`. keep actions event-sourced.
Kari: Runbook quick notes: 1) if auto-fallback triggers, page oncall, 2) check telemetry/trace links in the decision payload, 3) if repeated auto-fallbacks -> escalate to infra and model teams. I'll draft the runbook snippet.
Priya: Open questions for RFC follow-up: - how to sign/authorize intents between teams - minimal SLA for actuator latency (we don't want rollbacks to take >90s) - metric cardinality impact from probes - fallback variants: mirror-only vs full traffic swap
Sam: I'll prototype actuator API: `POST /actuate/fallback {canary_id, target_variant, decision_id}` returns 202 + operation_id. add `GET /actuate/status/{operation_id}`. will include idempotency token.
Ethan: We also need a 'graceful-degrade' action that reduces canary weight rather than full rollback for transient spikes. policy should support `action: reduce_weight -> from 10% to 2% over 30s`
Priya: Agreement: implement minimal watchtower (decision engine + audit) + actuator API + runbook updates. auto:true enabled for perf only with two-signal confirmation and 5m cooldown. correctness remains manual. I'll file RFC follow-up and PR for policy schema.
deploy-bot: Canary v3 at 10% -> steady.
Kari: I'll add oncall runbook page and include CLI examples and commands to unblock.
Sam: Filing a spike ticket to implement actuator contract and test harness. ETA 2 weeks.
Priya: Thanks all — closing sync. I'll link the RFC and the spike in the thread when created. :+1:
